data.logline: An arranged-cum-love marriage deteriorates into a bitter legal battle when clashing ideals of modern independence, social media validation, and traditional roles tear a young couple apart.
data.synopsis:
Siva and Sakthi enter into a modern arranged marriage that initially appears ideal. However, underlying tensions quickly emerge as Sakthi, influenced heavily by social media trends and radical feminist viewpoints, constantly clashes with Siva over household duties, financial independence, and personal boundaries. Their relationship disintegrates amidst constant arguments, public social media shaming, and irreconcilable ideological differences.

The couple eventually reaches the Family Welfare Court, advised by cunning lawyers like Narayanan and Lakshmi. What starts as petty marital disputes escalates into complex legal warfare involving domestic violence accusations, false claims, and societal judgment. As both families get dragged into the messy litigation, Siva and Sakthi experience the harsh realities of legal battles and separation.

After months of painful court proceedings, mutual realizations, and witnessing the misery of prolonged legal separation, both Siva and Sakthi begin to understand the compromises required in a relationship. In a climactic turnaround during their final hearing, Sakthi drops her divorce plea, signaling a tentative step toward reconciliation.

risks.summary: The second act features numerous recurring arguments over social media reels, household chores, and court dates that could slow down the narrative pace.
risks.evidence: Multiple montage sequences and repeated court hearing scenes covering similar interpersonal grievances.

charactersList.name: சிவா (Siva)
charactersList.description: An IT professional who marries Sakthi through an arranged-cum-love match, expecting a traditional and submissive partner, but struggles as she asserts her independence.
charactersList.goal: To maintain a comfortable, traditional marriage and resolve conflicts with his wife.
charactersList.motivation: Desire for peace, domestic harmony, and a predictable lifestyle.
charactersList.conflict: Clashes constantly with Sakthi over independence, division of household labor, social media culture, and personal choices.
charactersList.transformation: Evolves from an entitled and frustrated husband into a self-aware, remorseful partner willing to fight for his marriage and make mutual concessions.

charactersList.name: சக்தி (Sakthi)
charactersList.description: An independent, modern Gen Z woman with a feminist outlook who marries Siva, deeply affected by her traumatic past with her father.
charactersList.goal: To live life strictly on her own terms ('its my choice') without patriarchal control.
charactersList.motivation: Escaping generational patriarchal trauma and asserting absolute personal freedom and equality.
charactersList.conflict: Fights against Siva's expectations of traditional wifely duties and societal pressures from elders.
charactersList.transformation: Moves from rigid, defensive individualism to realizing the emotional toll of isolation, ultimately choosing to reconcile with Siva.

charactersList.name: நாராயணன் (Narayanan)
charactersList.description: Siva's cynical, street-smart divorce lawyer who handles matrimonial disputes with dark humor and cynical pragmatism.
charactersList.goal: To successfully navigate legal hurdles in Siva's divorce case while dealing with his own past.
charactersList.motivation: Professional duty blended with personal cynicism regarding modern relationships.
charactersList.conflict: Opposes Lakshmi in court while managing his own estranged relationship with his family.
charactersList.transformation: Gains emotional vulnerability upon hearing news of his own child through a phone call.

charactersList.name: லட்சுமி (Lakshmi)
charactersList.description: Sakthi's fierce, uncompromising feminist lawyer who is an ex-wife with a bitter personal history regarding men and marriage.
charactersList.goal: To win Sakthi's contested divorce and secure maximum legal and financial leverage.
charactersList.motivation: Radical feminist ideology fueled by personal trauma and a desire to dismantle patriarchal norms.
charactersList.conflict: Engages in intense courtroom and ideological battles against Narayanan and traditional family structures.
charactersList.transformation: Maintains her hardline stance throughout, though slightly challenged by Bharathi's perspective.

charactersList.name: சித்து (Sithu)
charactersList.description: Narayanan's associate and friend who assists Siva and Narayanan throughout the legal battle.
charactersList.goal: To assist Narayanan in legal proceedings and support Siva.
charactersList.conflict: Deals with the chaotic courtroom environment and police station standoffs.
charactersList.transformation: Remains a steady comedic and supportive sidekick.

charactersList.name: பழனிசாமி (Palanisamy)
charactersList.description: Sakthi's patriarchal, traditional father from Madurai who controlled his household and wife.
charactersList.goal: To marry off his daughter into a traditional setup and maintain social prestige.
charactersList.motivation: Adherence to traditional customs and parental authority.
charactersList.conflict: Clashes with Sakthi's modern, rebellious choices and estrangement.
charactersList.transformation: Humbled by the breakdown of his daughter's marriage and left helpless by her distance.

developmentNotes.title: Compress repetitive court hearing cycles

developmentNotes.before: Multiple nearly identical hearing/counselling intercuts with overlapping grievances.
developmentNotes.actionable: Keep 3 landmark hearings (filing, police escalation, final mutual chance) and fold the rest into a time-lapse montage song.

developmentNotes.title: Seed Narayanan’s personal subplot earlier

developmentNotes.before: Surprise child/video-call reveal without prior setup.

developmentNotes.title: Clarify Sakthi’s father trauma through one sharp flashback
developmentNotes.description: Palanisamy’s patriarchal control motivates Sakthi, but the wound can read as exposition-heavy.
developmentNotes.actionable: One 20–30s visual flashback tied to a present fight trigger (thaali / household order / permission).

draftComparison.current: Fast Gen-Z wedding satire shifts into dense courtroom procedural with many recurring hearings.

draftComparison.current: Script critiques both performative feminism and male entitlement, but some stretches risk reading as one-sided.
draftComparison.proposed: Pair every Sakthi excess beat with a Siva entitlement beat (and vice versa) inside the same sequence.
draftComparison.impact: Reduces polarization risk while keeping debate energy.
